entities.summary:
Muiredach Muinderg mac Forggo was a king of Ulaid from the Dál Fiatach. He was the son of Forgg mac Dalláin. His sobriquet means red-necked.

 Born around 440 CE, Muiredach Muinderg ascended to the throne in approximately 465 CE after his father's death. During his reign, he successfully navigated the complex web of alliances and rivalries between various Ulaid factions, ultimately maintaining stability and security for his kingdom.

 Muiredach Muinderg is notable for his diplomatic efforts with neighboring kingdoms, including a significant trade agreement with the kingdom of Dál Riata in modern-day Scotland. This deal not only strengthened economic ties but also facilitated cultural exchange and the spread of Christianity throughout Ulaid.

 His legacy extends beyond his own reign, as he played a crucial role in shaping the future of the Ulaid kingdom. Muiredach Muinderg's diplomatic achievements and strategic alliances laid the groundwork for subsequent generations of Ulaid rulers, ensuring the continuation of the Dál Fiatach dynasty.

 The annals of history recall Muiredach Muinderg as a king who skillfully balanced the competing interests of his people with the demands of an ever-changing world. His remarkable leadership and diplomatic prowess have inspired scholars and historians for centuries, offering a testament to the enduring power of effective governance.
